tagline: Drop a skill into **`.claude/skills/`** and it loads — **no marketplace**, no restart, and it can even **remove** tools.
summary: Extending Claude Code with a skill used to feel like packaging: build a plugin, register a marketplace, install it. Now a skill placed under **`.claude/skills/`** is **automatically loaded — no marketplace required**. **`/reload-skills`** re-scans the directories **without restarting** the session, so a skill you just added is usable immediately. And a skill (or slash command) isn't only additive: its frontmatter can set **`disallowed-tools`** to **remove tools** from the model while it's active.

sections.heading: No marketplace in the path
body: The friction people remember is the **distribution chain**: author a plugin, publish it to a marketplace, install and pin it. For a local skill that's all overhead.

Skills in **`.claude/skills/`** are now **discovered directly** — auto-loaded with **no marketplace required**. (`claude plugin init <name>` scaffolds one in place.) The directory *is* the registry; presence is registration.

sections.heading: Re-scan without restarting
body: Add or edit a skill and you don't have to bounce the session. **`/reload-skills`** re-scans the skill directories **in place**, so the new or changed skill is picked up mid-conversation.

This pairs with hooks: a **SessionStart** hook can return `reloadSkills: true` to trigger the same re-scan automatically. Either way, the skill set is a **live, reloadable** thing — not frozen at launch.

sections.heading: Skills can subtract, too
body: A skill's most surprising lever is **removal**. Frontmatter can declare **`disallowed-tools`**, and while that skill or slash command is active those tools are **taken away from the model**.

So a skill isn't only "here's a new capability." It can also be "for this task, **narrow** the surface" — dropping write access, or a risky tool, for the duration. Extensibility runs in **both directions**.

diagram.caption: Presence in `.claude/skills/` is registration. `/reload-skills` re-scans live; `disallowed-tools` lets an active skill **remove** tools.

nodes.label: Place a skill in .claude/skills/
nodes.note: A skill file on disk under `.claude/skills/`. No marketplace, no install step — the directory is the registry.

nodes.label: Directories auto-scanned
nodes.note: Claude Code scans the skill directories at startup — and on demand — discovering whatever is present **without marketplace registration**.

nodes.label: Skill loaded & available
nodes.note: The skill is now invocable. Getting here took only a file in the right place.

nodes.label: Invoked → frontmatter applies
nodes.note: When the skill runs, its frontmatter takes effect — including any tool restrictions it declares for the duration.

nodes.label: disallowed-tools removes tools
nodes.note: Frontmatter can **subtract**: listed tools are removed from the model while this skill or command is active. Extensibility that narrows, not only widens.

nodes.label: /reload-skills re-scans
nodes.note: Re-scan the directories **without restarting** the session — pick up a just-added skill mid-conversation. A SessionStart hook's `reloadSkills` does the same automatically.

scenarios.title: Drop a skill and it **loads** — no marketplace
scenarios.note: A file under `.claude/skills/` is discovered and invocable. The whole distribution chain collapses to "put it in the directory."

scenarios.title: A skill **removes** tools while active
scenarios.note: `disallowed-tools` in frontmatter takes tools away from the model for the duration — a skill scoping *down* the surface, not only adding to it.

scenarios.title: Pick up a new skill with **/reload-skills**
scenarios.note: Re-scan in place — no restart. A SessionStart hook returning `reloadSkills` triggers the same path automatically.

misconceptions.myth: A skill has to be packaged in a plugin and registered in a marketplace to be usable.
misconceptions.reality: Skills in **`.claude/skills/`** are auto-loaded — **no marketplace required**. Presence in the directory is registration.
misconceptions.why: Marketplaces are how shared plugins are distributed, so it's natural to assume they're the only path. For local skills the directory scan is enough.

misconceptions.myth: Adding or editing a skill means restarting the session.
misconceptions.reality: **`/reload-skills`** re-scans the skill directories **without a restart**, and a SessionStart hook can trigger the same re-scan via `reloadSkills`.
misconceptions.why: Most config is read once at launch, so a skill set feels frozen. Here it's explicitly reloadable mid-session.

misconceptions.myth: A skill can only add capability — more tools, more commands.
misconceptions.reality: A skill or slash command can set **`disallowed-tools`** to **remove** tools from the model while it's active. Extensibility runs both ways.
misconceptions.why: "Extension" implies addition. The subtractive direction — narrowing the surface for a task — is easy to overlook but just as real.
